(BY SHRI AMIT PANDEY - PANEL LAWYER)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER
This is the first application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in FIR No.47/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Narmadapuram, for the offence under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that a false complaint has been made by the prosecutrix against the present applicant alleging commission of rape with her.

He submits that however, an application was submitted by the prosecutrix to the Police Station Naramadapuram on 06.04.2022 (Annexure A/2) wherein it was mentioned by her that for creating pressure upon the applicant so as to get married with her, the prosecutrix had made a false complaint of committing rape and ultimately,

sentences.text: when the applicant refused to get married with her, she made a complaint to the police.

In that application, the prosecutrix had very categorically admitted that the present applicant had neither developed any physical relation with her nor she is inclined to make any report against him.
The said application was submitted in the police station and the acknowledgment of Station House Officer, Itarsi is also there.

He further submits that considering the whole scenario of the case,
prima facie, it can be presumed that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in the alleged crime.

4. O n the other hand, counsel for State has opposed the prayer of anticipatory bail and submitted that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. also, the prosecutrix has made allegation against the present applicant and, therefore, the applicant is not inclined to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
5. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
7. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 438 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE rao Amar Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5578866/
